$description: taha-portfolio — concept `as-built`. Machine-readable sibling of DIRECTION.md. FORMAT: Design Tokens Community Group (DTCG) format, pinned to the Community Group Draft of 30 July 2026. This is NOT a W3C Recommendation and calling it 'the W3C design token standard' would be wrong in the same checkable way as a fabricated citation; the value shapes have already changed between drafts, which is why the draft is pinned by date. LIMITS, stated rather than worked around: (1) `dimension` is an object {value, unit} and the unit set is CLOSED to `px` and `rem` — no em, no %, no pt, no dp. (2) `duration` is likewise an object, numeric value plus ms or s. (3) THEREFORE THIS IS A WEB ARTIFACT. Apple specifies in pt and Material in dp/sp and neither is expressible in a DTCG dimension. That costs nothing in this run because the platform mode is `neutral` — web only, no native surface — so there are no pt or dp values to lose. Any later native surface puts its numbers in DIRECTION.md prose or in $extensions, never silently rounded into px. (4) The paired colour token (swatch + its legal foreground + the measured ratio) is a CONVENTION THIS PLUGIN IMPOSES, not one the format enforces — DTCG has no pair type. It is modelled here as a group of two colour tokens with a $description binding them and recording the measured ratio. (5) UNSETTLED: the `color` value shape in this draft — hex string versus a colorSpace-plus-components object — was not confirmed against the primary source. Colours are written as hex strings below and DIRECTION.md is authoritative for colour until that is confirmed. Naming this gap is what stops a later reader building on it. Every ratio here was independently recomputed in Loop 2 from the WCAG relative-luminance formula; twelve of thirteen reproduced Loop 1 exactly and the thirteenth (the focus-ring flip) was corrected — see color.cyanotype.focus-ring-on-accent.

com.inter-face.run.gate: written at Loop 2, presented at Gate B, not yet signed
com.inter-face.run.modes: two art directions by print convention — cyanotype (dark) and diazo (light). NOT one palette inverted. Line weights change with the mode; that is the whole of the mode work.
com.inter-face.run.accentSampledFrom: ~/Documents/madeintaha-portfolio/css/style.css custom-property block, lines 14-54 — the subject's own shipped-but-unlaunched portfolio, re-read at run time

space.$description: Base unit 4px, the drafting grid. Steps are named by their multiple of the base, so space.24 is 24 x 4px = 96px. Absent numbers are deliberately absent — a step with no job gets no token. SEPARATE BINDING RULE, not expressible here: any pair of adjacent interactive targets holds an 8px minimum gap, because a 16px glyph plus an 8px gap is exactly 24px centre-to-centre and clears the spacing route; a 6px gap fails and the visual difference is two pixels.

1.$description: vertical rhythm unit; schedule cell padding

2.$description: minimum gap between adjacent inline affordances

3.$description: title-block cell inset; narrow-viewport drawn border

24.$description: title-block band height, and the scroll-padding-block-end that keeps it from obscuring a jumped-to section

target-min.$description: minimum interactive target, both axes. The Size route, not the Spacing exception — clears 2.5.8's 24x24 with room and needs no per-pair geometry proof

icon.$description: icon glyph size. Icon size and target size are INDEPENDENT decisions: a 20px icon inside a 44px target is correct, a 20px icon that IS the target is a failure

icon-canvas.$description: drawing canvas for a custom glyph, with a 20px live area and 2px padding

measure-body.$description: NOT DIRECTLY EXPRESSIBLE. The body measure is 60ch, and `ch` is not in DTCG's closed unit set. This value is a placeholder that MUST NOT be consumed as rem — see $extensions.unexpressible

stroke.$description: Line weights change with the mode; that is the whole of the mode work in this direction. Do not reuse one token across both modes.

diazo-secondary.$description: prototype-verified to render at DPR 1 as a grid gap rather than vanishing or snapping to 1px

icon.$description: cyanotype. Diazo icon stroke is 1.5px, matching the drawing's own retune — a deliberate divergence from Material's grade rule, reasoned in DIRECTION.md §13

radius.$description: Zero at every step. A drawing has no radii. The concentric rule (inner = outer - gap) is in use and degenerates to 0 at every nesting level because the outer is 0. A builder who reads this and adds a 4px radius to an input has broken both the rule and the direction.

sheet.$description: ONE family across all six roles. A drawing sheet is lettered in one lettering set; a second family reads as a second draftsman, and the document's authority rests on one hand having made both the drawing and the correction. Roles separate by case, tracking and weight, never by a second face. WARNING: see $extensions.fontWeightGap — the vendored files do not contain every weight this scale names.

body.$description: SPECIFIED 400. RENDERS FROM THE 500 FILE — no 400 file is vendored. Measured by advance width: w400 and w500 probe strings are both 217.31px. This makes RISK 3 worse than Loop 1 assumed

field.$description: SPECIFIED 600. RENDERS FROM THE 700 FILE — w600 and w700 both 221.31px

size.$description: ROLE-INDEXED, NOT RATIO-GENERATED. There is no modular ratio and claiming one would be a fabrication — a drawing sheet's lettering set is a fixed series of named heights. Adjacent-step ratios are 1.083, 1.231, 1.063, 1.059, then a deliberate jump of 2.22x: a drawing has lettering, and it has a sheet title, and nothing in between.

field.$description: 13px — title-block fields and schedule cells, caps

redline.$description: 16px — the correction voice. Specified 500 italic; NO ITALIC FILE IS VENDORED, so it renders as a synthesised oblique (italic and upright advances both 204.53px)

body.$description: 17px — notes and accounts. The RISK 3 size

title-min.$description: 40px — lower bound of the h1 clamp

title-max.$description: 72px — upper bound of the h1 clamp. The fluid middle is 5vw and is not expressible as a DTCG dimension

tracking.$description: NOT EXPRESSIBLE AS SPECIFIED. Tracking is authored in `em` and DTCG's dimension unit set is closed to px and rem. Values below are the px equivalents AT THEIR OWN ROLE'S SIZE and are correct only at that size — do not reuse them across sizes. The em values are authoritative in DIRECTION.md §7.

motion.$description: There is exactly ONE piece of narrative motion in this design: the redline draw-on. Everything else on all six surfaces is static, and keeping it that small is deliberate. Two rules that do not fork: nothing animates above the fold (the hero redline is painted at rest from first paint), and motion never gates information (every redline's text is readable before, during and after the draw).

draw-sheet.$description: full-width sheet correction — the longest single stroke in the design

exit.$description: shorter than every enter. A departure that takes as long as an arrival reads as lag

stagger-cap.$description: total stagger ceiling, so the 5th and later redlines carry no additional delay and six corrections never take six seconds

draw.$description: enter curve. Named once, referenced by every transition that uses it

redline-draw.$description: The redline draw-on. Animates stroke-dashoffset. Triggered by IntersectionObserver at threshold 0.4 with rootMargin '0px 0px -15% 0px' — NEVER a scroll listener. Stagger 90ms, capped at 360ms. ONLY runs below the fold.

com.inter-face.reducedMotion.state: Both inks at full opacity from first paint, and the redline's stroke ends rendered SQUARED (stroke-linecap: butt) rather than round. The squared end is what makes it read as drawn and finished rather than as caught mid-draw. A viewer who never saw the full version cannot tell anything is missing.
com.inter-face.reducedMotion.honoredAt: both layers — the CSS media query AND matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') in JS with a change listener, so a mid-session preference change is respected
com.inter-face.reducedMotion.appleFiveTechniques: checked: no z-axis depth transition anywhere, and nothing animates into or out of a blur. Those are the two nobody removes; there was nothing to remove because neither was ever used.
com.inter-face.reducedMotion.compositorNote: stroke-dashoffset is NOT a compositor property and animates on the main thread. Recorded as a broken rule in DIRECTION.md §25 with its cost, not waved through.

unexpressible.$description: Values this design uses that a DTCG dimension cannot hold. Listed so a build tool fails loudly rather than silently rounding. A token file that quietly turns 60ch into 60rem has produced a wrong layout with a valid schema.
unexpressible.measure-60ch: body measure is 60ch — `ch` is outside the closed px/rem unit set. size.measure-body is a placeholder and must not be consumed as rem.
unexpressible.h1-fluid-middle: clamp(2.5rem, 5vw, 4.5rem) — the 5vw term is a viewport unit and is not expressible. Only the two bounds are tokenised.
unexpressible.tracking-em: all tracking is authored in em; font.tracking holds px equivalents valid ONLY at each role's own size.
unexpressible.hairline-opacity: the S3 hairline mesh is line-secondary at 12% opacity, 24px pitch — an opacity, not a dimension.
unexpressible.native-units: none in this run. Platform mode is `neutral` (web only), so there are no pt or dp values being lost. A later native surface puts them in DIRECTION.md prose or here, never rounded into px.

fontWeightGap.$description: MEASURED IN LOOP 2, UNRESOLVED AT GATE B. The vendored Cabinet Grotesk files contain weights 500, 700 and 800 ONLY — no 400, no 600, no italic. Proven by advance-width comparison, because document.fonts.check() returns true for every weight (it matches by NEAREST AVAILABLE FACE) and therefore cannot detect this. The obvious detection method silently lies.
fontWeightGap.body-400: renders from the 500 file — w400 and w500 probe strings both 217.31px
fontWeightGap.field-600: renders from the 700 file — w600 and w700 both 221.31px
fontWeightGap.redline-italic: synthesised oblique — italic and upright both 204.53px; a real italic face changes advances
fontWeightGap.cost: body copy ships heavier than specified in a display face at 17px, which makes RISK 3 unmitigated rather than accepted. Fix requires acquiring 400 + a true italic AND subsetting to Latin, because the unsubset addition takes tier 1 from ~79KB to ~118KB, over the 100KB ceiling.

budget.tier1Estimate: ~80,800 bytes (~79KB) — fonts 60,764 measured, HTML+CSS ~18,000 gz inferred, JS ~2,000 gz inferred
budget.tier2: 0 bytes — declared as a number. This run has no tier-2 layer: nothing was assigned from CRAFT.md's Rendering-and-GPU or heavy post-processing groups, and the only tier-2 byte in the design (Surface 5's raster, 11,884 bytes) was cut at Gate B review.
budget.lcp: NOT MEASURED — no throttled device was reachable in this run. Stated as an open number, not claimed as a pass.
budget.evidenceCeiling: No CPU-throttling instrument was reachable and the synthetic-load substitute was verified not to bite (an 8ms per-frame burn fits inside a ~11ms frame budget). Every performance claim in this run caps at PARTIAL.
